newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica trade balance on track, exports disappoint.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica trade balance on track, exports disappoint.

text.p: South Africa recorded another trade surplus in April, which economists said indicated that exports were picking up steam although there was still much room for improvement.

South African Revenue Service figures released on Tuesday showed a trade surplus of 725 million rand in April from a healthy 1.98 billion rand surplus in March and a 451.6 million rand deficit in February.
On the export side there were increases in the key categories including mineral and chemical products, precious and base metals and machinery and transport.
But figures showed that imports were also growing quite strongly with pick-ups in most of the manufactured categories.

"We have a situation whereby imports are up by about seven percent year-on-year in monthly terms and exports are six percent up and that's pretty mediocre," said EW Balderson economist Mike Schussler.
He said it was important to note that imports flowing in were also more consumer orientated, ending up in grocery stores and individual households.

"In general I'm a bit disappointed with the export figures because the last six months in export growth have been mainly in manufactured goods and what we've seen this month is very much the primary good category such as vegetables and minerals," Schussler noted.
On the imports side, growth in manufactured categories indicated there was a lot of strength in the economy and that interst rates were therefore unlikely to come down soon, Schussler said.

Viewed on a three-month rolling basis, economists said it was likely imports would continue to grow but they were hopeful that a pick-up in overseas manufacturing sales would aid South African exports.
